headline: Data center moratorium recommended to City Council; 37 Enon Street apartment hearing continued to November 17.
summary: The meeting covered a proposed temporary moratorium on data centers and a plan for 179 apartments and retail space at the existing Stop & Shop site, 37 Enon Street. The moratorium was recommended to City Council. The 37 Enon Street hearing was continued to November 17.
decisions: Recommended that the Clean Energy Advisory Committee review the 37 Enon Street project (6-1).
Continued the 37 Enon Street public hearing to November 17 (7-0).
Set a November 17 public hearing on the 38 Stanley Street site plan review (7-0).
Recommended to City Council a temporary moratorium on data centers until November 30th, 2027 (7-0).
discussion: Data center moratorium: Members said the city needs time to define data centers and study impacts, such as power and water use, before deciding where or whether to allow them.
37 Enon Street parking: Members discussed a special permit to cut required parking from 367 to 281 spaces. Residents worried that cars would spill onto nearby neighborhood streets.
37 Enon Street traffic: Residents questioned the traffic study and said Enon Street and Route 1A are already congested. The applicant said traffic would drop by more than half.
37 Enon Street lighting and noise: Residents near the railroad raised concerns about rear lighting, noise, and possible sound barriers.
Climate review of projects: Members discussed asking the Clean Energy Advisory Committee to review projects against the city's Climate Action Plan.
